bbc.title: French protesters return to the streets
bbc.summary: Protests against poor economic conditions have been held across France. Nearly 1,000 people have been arrested after clashes with riot police in cities including Paris and Marseilles. Also: campaigning intensifies ahead of the US mid-term elections. We have a special report from the Rio Grande Valley in South Texas. Gianni Infantino claims the "vast majority" supports his bid for re-election as head of world football's governing body, FIFA. Final rallies are held in Brazil ahead of Sunday's presidential run-off election between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro. One man has been arrested after Hitler's Eagle's Nest retreat in Bavaria was engulfed in flames. And Europe's busiest shopping street, Oxford Street in London, prepares to go traffic free. The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. Listen for the latest headlines and current affairs from around the world. Politics, economics, climate, business, technology, health – we cover it all with expert analysis and insight. bbc.title: The Happy Pod: Lost my ring, found some friends
bbc.summary: Patrick Mohr thought his wedding ring was gone after it fell off his hand while he swam in Italy, but it led to an international friendship with three locals who dived to find it. Filippo Palagi, Nicola Malloggi and Edoardo Poggi went on a trip to return it to Patrick in Ireland. Also: the grandmother who competed at Miss Great Britain and made history in the process. Glamour Gran Ann wants other women to see that getting older does not mean disappearing. In Australia, the reporter who ended up saving a man's life while covering floods in Brisbane. ABC reporter Will Murray pulled a man from a sinking car, after the driver accidentally drove into the flood. Plus - World Athletics are holding their first ever World Treadmill Championship. And the live stream in Finland where you can watch puppies 24/7. Image: The three men who helped Patrick find his ring, posing with Patrick holding it. Credit: Patrick Mohr. Our weekly collection of inspiring, uplifting and happy news from around the world. Presenter: Holly Gibbs. Music composed by Iona Hampson

bbc.title: Melania Trump brokers ceasefire for Ukrainian city
bbc.summary: The White House says the US first lady, Melania Trump, has brokered a local ceasefire for a frontline city in a Russian-occupied part of Ukraine. The truce in Oleshky, in the Kherson region, is due to begin on October 29. The White House says the city is on "the brink of disaster" without medicine, food and clean water. Residents of the city have resorted to eating garden weeds to survive. Also: Donald Trump files a lawsuit seeking to block Alaska's result in the midterms if the Republican incumbent does not win his Senate seat. We look at the legacy of the iPod as the device turns 25. The company behind ChatGPT announces that it will no longer train its AI models live on the internet amid security concerns. Brazilians go to the polls on Sunday in what’s predicted to be an incredibly close presidential election. And the hunt for the next James Bond is underway, with screen tests rumoured to be taking place in London. The Global News Podcast brings you the breaking news you need to hear, as it happens. bbc.title: Sudan's hospitals deliberately targeted by RSF fighters
bbc.summary: A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed El-Fasher's healthcare system during their long siege and subsequent takeover of the city in Darfur a year ago. UN human rights chief Volker Türk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes. Also: the Israeli military says two soldiers were killed in an attack by Palestinian gunmen in the occupied West Bank. The two suspected attackers were shot dead by the IDF. Ukrainian defence officials say there are still restrictions on their use of the Starshield satellite network, despite President Trump saying it was operating normally. bbc.title: Yemen's humanitarian crisis
bbc.summary: Our senior international corrrespondent Orla Guerin reports from Yemen where fighting has intensified between government forces and Houthi rebels. chronicle.summary: News Connect 文化欄、今回のゲストは、小説家の王谷晶さんです。ダガー賞翻訳部門を受賞した『ババヤガの夜』でも注目の王谷さん。今回は、作家になるまでの道のりを伺いました。北関東の田舎で本と録画ビデオに囲まれて育った幼少期から、二次創作、海外文学との出会い、ライターから小説家への転換など。そして、王谷作品の強度を支える、「徹底的に刈り込む」執筆スタイルについてもお聞きしています。 ▼ゲスト 王谷晶（小説家） 1981年、東京都生まれ。2021年、『ババヤガの夜』が日本推理作家協会賞・長編部門の最終候補に。同作の英訳版『The Night of Baba Yaga』（翻訳：サム・ベット）が、2025年7月ダガー賞翻訳部門を日本人として初めて受賞。同作は、アメリカのLGBTQ＋文学における最高峰とされるラムダ文学賞ミステリー部門にもノミネートされた。その他の著書に『完璧じゃない、あたしたち』『君の六月は凍る』『カラダは私の何なんだ？』『令和元年生まれ ルリカ50歳』など。 ▼MC 岩井圭也（小説家） X： ⁠⁠⁠https://x.com/keiya_iwai⁠⁠ ▼News Connect 土曜版・日曜版・夕刊版 Spotifyプレイリストはこちら 🟢土曜版 ⁠⁠https://open.spotify.com/playlist/3MKhzjyNlx96n2Khmt35EK⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ 🔴日曜版 ⁠⁠https://open.spotify.com/playlist/2cAjmNYGXvSXCtPujQSNVb⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ 🔵夕刊版 国際欄 https://open.spotify.com/playlist/3CtpYOPniQT6FEuByBdfg3 🟣夕刊版 文化欄 ⁠⁠⁠ https://open.spotify.com/playlist/6DSiNeJQwWhV982h3BxOyg 🟡夕刊版 金融欄 ⁠ https://open.spotify.com/playlist/4btihPGM3vOhndcdtzQTtM ▼支援プログラム「Chronicleサポーター」については、こちらをご参照ください。 https://chronicle-inc.net/support LISTENで開く
